recipes.name: Krista's Sticky Honey Garlic Wings
ingredients_raw: 24 chicken wings, split and tips discarded

steps.text: Preheat the oven to 375 degrees F (190 degrees C).
Arrange chicken wings evenly on a baking sheet.
Bake in the preheated oven until crisp, 35 to 45 minutes. Transfer wings to a baking dish and set aside.

Mix together 2 1/2 cups water, brown sugar, soy sauce, honey, garlic, and ginger in a medium saucepan over medium-high heat; bring to a boil. Whisk together remaining 3/4 cup water and cornstarch in a small bowl until smooth; stir into soy sauce mixture and cook until thickened. Pour sauce over chicken wings to coat.

Return wings to the oven and bake until sauce is bubbling and chicken is no longer pink at the bone and the juices run clear, 15 to 20 minutes. An instant-read thermometer inserted into the center should read at least 165 degrees F (74 degrees C).

raw_recipe.headline: Krista's Sticky Honey Garlic Wings
raw_recipe.description: These wings with honey garlic sauce are baked in the oven for a healthy appetizer that's just as sweet, sticky, and delicious as the fried version.

review.reviewBody: These wings are wonderful. Everyone in my house loved them. I made them as written except I only mixed about 4 tbsp. water with the cornstarch. I think 3/4 of a cup would be too much and the sauce would not thicken up nicely. I will definitely be making this recipe again.

This was such a hit for our Big Game party last night. Even my husband, who isn't a wing eater, gave very high compliments on this sauce! I will definitely be making this again! 

I cooked my wings in the instant pot and finished them under the broiler using the sauce recipe you have given. I topped the wings off with some red pepper flakes to add just a bit of heat to the sweet. BEST wings I have ever had!

I doubled these for a party and the guests liked them but I thought they were too sweet as written. 
Made these adjustments for sticky wing perfection:
*I didn't fry the wings but dusted in seasoned flour and baked at 375 for 40 minuted. Wings perfectly cooked.
*Before I added the sauce to the wings I gave a splash of rice wine vinegar and lime juice (to balance the sweet) and 1/4 cup of toasted sesame seeds. Boiled a little longer until thick...
It tasted just like the sesame chicken at our favorite asian cafe here in town.

they turned out great...having read reviews on the water amounts....I used 1 cup total...I made syrup with 3/4 cup water...mixed cornstarch in 1/4 cup and then added that too...AWESOME and very sticky =0)
Thanks for the recipe =0)

Fabulous, except . . . Cut the soya sauce in half, otherwise it's too Teriyaki-type falvoured. I made one set with no soya sauce and it was great as well, just a nice sweet honey garlic vs. tangy honey garlic with the soya sauce. Neither time, did I mix the extra 3/4 cup of water in with the cornstarch; I just used some of the hot sauce, as I felt there was enough water in this recipe and I wanted to max the flavour.

Also, pouring the sauce over the wings wastes a lot of sauce. I dunk the wings in the sauce and then bake 10 minutes, redunk again with the rest of the sauce and finish baking. Then the wings are nice and saucy and the least amount of sauce is wasted on the pan. I put a layer of tinfoil down and spray it with Pam. Then they don't stick to the pan much, if at all. Definitely a keeper recipe!!!

I enjoyed the sauce as I like my wings sweet. Before baking the wings I sprinkled them with a little salt, black pepper and garlic powder for some extra flavor. I also reduced the water from 3/4 cup to 1/4 cup when mixing in 3 tbsp cornstarch to thicken sauce. I think 3/4 cup water would have made sauce too runny.

This recipe was delicious. I left out the cornstarch process. I added crushed red peppers to my meat seasoning, I baked my wings @350 for 40 mins and then poured the sauce on top, mixed and let the sauce marinate into the meat. For the sauce I used less soy (about 2-3 tbs) and the same measurements of honey & water (NO brown sugar). I also used minced garlic instead. This was a hit, My family loved it.

There has been comments that the sauce is not as thick as they would like. 
I (accidentally) added the cornstarch right into the sauce that was boiling on the stove. I also made the separate cornstarch and water mixture and added them together. The sauce was PERFECT! Sticky, yet not runny. It was great. Instead of using 3 tbsp cornstarch, use 6! It was very yummy

Great flavor but needed to add extra honey and hot sauce to give them more of a kick. Also had to turn oven up to 425 to get them to crisp, we don't like chewy wings, we like them crispy. Also, ended up putting them back on the cookie sheet to get some of the sauce away from them because they will not crisp when they are sitting in a bunch of sauce. Will likely make them again because we did like the flavor.

I used this recipe and I love it ... I added just a little more cornstarch to make it a bit thicker,an extra tbsp of honey, a little cayenne pepper, two extra cloves of garlic and regular soy sauce... I let the chicken cook uncovered for a while to let the sauce cook on and then I put the chicken in the bottom broiler to give it a bit of crispiness on top and it came out absolutely scrumptious!

Waaaaayyyyyy too much water! I'd cut it in half and instead of baking them again I would put them in an electric skillet. I poured out a ton of watery sauce and the skin on the wings were mushy still.

Just about perfect as written. I added salt, pepper and garlic powder to the drumettes that we used. To the sauce I added a splash of lime juice, rice vinegar and about 1/2 tsp of toasted sesame oil and cut back on the sugar and water. These were over the top. I've served as a starter and as an entree with hibachi rice. Thanks for a great recipe.
It did not thicken up at all! I ended up adding a rue to thicken and I didn't use all the water! Had to add more garlic and honey tho quite a bit more honey and garlic. Taste was great tho!
Delicious I made these for my very picky girls and they just ate them up. Only change would add a bit more corn starch to make a bit thicker.
We no longer order in wings. Easy to make & family loves them. Add a dash of hot sauce to liven it up!
My husband loved it, it was easy to make. When I turned the wings over I added a thin line on Honey.
I love it. I made the sauce with spare ribs and my family loves it. It’s a new family favourite.
I didn’t use as much water and thickener as suggested and it still didn’t thicken up
This was just ok. It wasn’t sticky, it was very watery. It needs a lot less water & red pepper flakes and/or sriracha sauce.
The sauce was delicious but it doesn't stay on the wings well. Next time, I plan to coat the wings in flour prior to pouring the sauce on top of the wings to help the sauce stick.
